message.content: {"6860_8353801560028": {"answer": "B", "reason": "Pulmonary sequestration most commonly affects the left lower lobe and often presents as a mass with an air-fluid level due to secondary infection or communication with the bronchial tree."}, "6860_8353801567689": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The imaging demonstrates a retrocardiac lesion in the left lower lobe with an air-fluid level, compensatory emphysema (hyperinflation), and a dilated azygos vein indicating systemic venous drainage typical of sequestration."}, "6860_8353801567905": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The combination of a retrocardiac left lower lobe lesion with an air-fluid level, compensatory emphysema, and a dilated systemic feeding/draining vessel is characteristic of pulmonary sequestration."}, "6860_8353801568016": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The diagnosis is pulmonary sequestration based on the classic triad of a retrocardiac left lower lobe opacity with air-fluid levels, adjacent hyperinflation, and evidence of anomalous systemic vasculature."}}
